insight.title: Why prices are actually invisible signals
insight.subtitle: How a simple number helps coordinate the entire global economy.

sections.text: Imagine prices as secret messages sent across the globe. They tell businesses what people want and how much is available. When a price rises, it signals that an item is becoming rare or more popular. This helps companies decide what to make next. Without these signals, our modern world would simply stop working.

When many people want the same pair of shoes, the price goes up. This happens because there are not enough shoes for everyone. The higher cost forces some people to wait. Meanwhile, the extra profit encourages factories to produce more. Eventually, the supply increases, and the price starts to fall back down again.

This simple system coordinates billions of people without any single person being in charge. It ensures that bread reaches grocery stores and fuel reaches gas stations every day. Markets use prices to move resources exactly where they are needed most. It is a beautiful, invisible dance that keeps our global economy moving forward.

news.title: Pakistan's economic mismanagement pushes poverty, inequality to record highs
news.description: : Pakistan's poverty rate has soared to 29%, the highest in 11 years, while income inequality has climbed to its worst level in nearly three decades, exposing deep cracks in the country's economic management. According to a government survey, nearly 70 million Pakistanis now live below the monthly poverty threshold of Rs8,484, as reported by The Express Tribune.
